fact_notes: Home UPS units in Pakistan are mostly offline/standby (or line-interactive) inverters: on mains, a relay connects the load to the mains and a charger keeps the battery topped up; when mains fails the relay switches the load to the inverter. The relay makes the audible click (Wikipedia 'Uninterruptible power supply'; propakistani.pk UPS buying guide).
Transfer time of standby UPS is typically a few to ~20 milliseconds; 'computer mode' UPS ~10 ms (Wikipedia; Schneider Electric FAQ).
A battery gives DC (one direction); the inverter converts it to AC like the grid, which in Pakistan is 50 Hz = 50 back-and-forth cycles a second.
A human blink lasts about 100-400 ms (Harvard BioNumbers 100706), so a ~10-20 ms switch is far faster than a blink; the fan's own spin carries it through the gap.
